LLM auditresponse for nodechem-studio.js:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided JavaScript file `nodechem-studio.js` is a runtime override script commonly used in Electron-based applications to redirect the `resourcesPath` and filesystem operations to a custom application directory. It determines the app directory by parsing command-line arguments (`--app`), inspecting the process entry point, or falling back to environment variables like `_APPDIR`. It then patches the `process.resourcesPath` and wraps several `fs` and `fs.promises` methods to redirect file operations from the default Electron resources path to the resolved application directory.

The code does not perform any network requests, execute external commands, or engage in obfuscated behavior. It uses standard Node.js APIs (`fs`, `path`) to implement filesystem redirection, which is a legitimate technique in Electron packaging to support custom installation layouts (e.g., in Linux distributions). The conditional environment variable settings (`ELECTRON_IS_DEV`, `NODE_ENV`) are based on local filesystem checks and are used to enforce production mode when running from a packaged app. No data exfiltration, remote code execution, or suspicious system modifications are present.

This script appears to be a packaging helper for integrating an Electron app into a system-wide installation (e.g., under `/usr/lib`), consistent with distribution packaging practices. While it manipulates Node.js internals, it does so transparently and for a legitimate runtime integration purpose.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Legitimate Electron app path redirection; no malicious behavior</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for nodechem-studio.sh:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided script `nodechem-studio.sh` is a launcher script for an Electron-based application. It sets up environment variables such as `_APPDIR`, `CHROME_DESKTOP`, and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to ensure the application runs in the correct context. It then determines the location of the application entry point by checking for the presence of `app.asar`, `app`, or `app.asar.unpacked` in the application directory. This is standard behavior for Electron apps that use ASAR packaging.

The script conditionally disables the Electron sandbox when running as root (unless `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` is set), which is a known workaround but documented and expected in certain environments. It also supports Ozone platform selection (X11/Wayland) via an environment variable derived from the app name, falling back to auto if unspecified. All of these behaviors are consistent with standard Electron app packaging and deployment practices on Linux.

There are no network operations, no use of `curl`, `wget`, `eval`, `base64`, or `exec` with dynamic content, and no file system manipulations beyond locating the app bundle. The `exec` call is used safely to launch Electron with predefined arguments, including a required bootstrap script and the app path. The script does not exfiltrate data, download remote code, or modify system state. It operates entirely within the application's own directory and uses only environment variables and local paths.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Standard Electron app launcher, no malicious behavior
</summary>
</security_assessment>
